reviews.scope: PDF abstract, introduction, sections 2.1-2.3, equations (10),(11),(14), theorem 2.2 inspected. Numerical imaging section not reviewed.
reviews.finding: Exact pre-existing algorithm. beta=1 connects RAAR, HPR, AAR and a difference-map instance; beta!=1 is not that difference-map family. Convex conclusions do not automatically extend to two nonconvex circles.

reviews.scope: arXiv v3 2018, pages 1-9 and 13-18 read as extracted text; local proof pages 10-12 inspected only in part. Figure pixels not yet inspected.
reviews.finding: Line/ellipse and line/p-sphere examples have periodic domains and long complicated transients. Circle-line singular-set irregular behavior was already reported. Attractive domains and transient paths must not be confused with a persistent strange attractor. DOI final publication 10.1007/s11228-017-0457-0.

reviews.scope: arXiv v2, 36 pages. Example 2.7, Examples 3.9 and 3.17, Remark 3.14, Section 5 pages 29-35 read; full general convergence proof not independently audited.
reviews.finding: RAAR, also relaxed Douglas-Rachford, on TWO PLANAR CIRCLES is explicitly prior art, including intersecting, separated, nested, concentric and tangent cases. Local convergence statements need their hypotheses; do not imply global convergence of our noncoplanar 3D configurations. Published SIAM J Optimization 30(1),542-584 (2020), DOI 10.1137/18M1229638.

reviews.scope: Publisher-indexed abstract and body excerpts including strange-attractor discussion read. Direct DOI open unavailable; PMC challenge not bypassed. Not a full-paper review.
reviews.finding: Strange-attractor search dynamics in projection/difference-map methods were explicitly proposed. This excludes any claim to discover chaos in constraint-search algorithms in general.

reviews.scope: Institutional full figure-5 caption and indexed text read; full article not yet reviewed.
reviews.finding: Two circles used as a UNION constituting one constraint, with a line as the other. This differs from two separate noncoplanar spatial circle constraints, but establishes elementary circle examples and failure mechanisms as prior art.

reviews.scope: Publisher chapter excerpt only, not full book.
reviews.finding: Nonconvex projection chaos is established background, not a new mechanism claim.

reviews.scope: Original RAAR.py, Algorithm constructor and computeRelaxation, cell type and LICENSE inspected; all relevant evaluator source pinned and copied verbatim.
reviews.finding: Our map matches the published evaluator. Four 400000-step upstream runs remain nonperiodic with positive leading finite growth. R820 has positive mean second growth but one 10000-step window is negative, so uniform positivity at every observed window length is not claimed. The installed imaging framework was not invoked.

conclusion: No exact match to the six recorded noncoplanar circle cases located in this bounded search. This is neither proof of priority nor an exhaustive equivalence classification. Existing algorithm, planar-circle studies and projection chaos must be credited.
open_gaps: A complete review of earlier projection-algorithm chaos papers and supplementary material
